doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Don Costa and the difficulty of writing charts on guitar
summary: Don Costa as a guitarist who arranged for Sinatra; Pallo says writing music is hard on guitar.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who, can you think of a songwriter that you like that works from the guitar? I mean most of those guys played the piano.
That’s right. And I can’t remember the name now — Costa. Don Costa, who wrote a lot for Sinatra.
And he wrote a lot of great arrangements. That was one now you just mentioned, that’s a guitar player that wrote a lot of arrangements and great arrangements. And it’s just hard

to write because sometimes if I — going back when I did write some charts, you have your hand on here and you’re here, and now you have to grab the pencil and you’re doing this, and it’s so hard, whereas a lot of pianists, as you play piano, you can go like this and you could write it down.

But on the guitar it’s so hard, because you have the pick in your hand too, so you have to use your thumb instead and then try to write. So it’s kind of tough. But you get by on that. But Don Costa is the only one that I know of. I’ll have to ask some of the guitar players that I know, and he did write some great arrangements for Sinatra.
